chapter_title: Vừa về đến nhà, Giang Niên mở tủ lạnh thì hơi lạnh phả vào mặt

segments.title: Vừa về đến nhà, Giang Niên mở tủ lạnh thì hơi lạnh phả vào mặt
segments.content:
Zhennan was a small county town in the south, where the late summer heat was unbearable.

Jiang Nian had just returned home when the refrigerator door was opened, and a white mist billowed out.

He searched for a while, finally finding the few slices of bread left over from the morning, and took a few bites to get by. With something in his stomach, he finally recovered.

Buzzzzz. His phone vibrated. Someone was calling him.

It was Le Zhi, the class life committee member—that pimply-faced show-off. This dude had added everyone in class on QQ, claiming it was to foster class unity, but in reality, he was just after the girls in his own backyard.

"Jiang Nian, Zhou Yuting is looking for people to hang out. She asked me to see if you want to go," Le Zhi's voice held a hint of persuasion. He had once said that he liked Zhou Yuting.

To be precise, few boys in the class didn't like Zhou Yuting, Jiang Nian included.

Zhou Yuting had a melon-seed face and willow-leaf eyebrows, a slender waist, and long legs. Beneath her summer school uniform was a soft, youthful swell. She was smart and rich, the class's academic representative.

"Not going."

"For real? Are you still hung up on what happened at her birthday party?" Le Zhi pressed. "Come on, it's not like she did it on purpose. It was just a joke."

The mere mention of the birthday party made Jiang Nian's temper flare.

Not long ago, Zhou Yuting had celebrated her birthday, and six or seven of them had gathered for a meal.

Out of kindness, Jiang Nian had taken the initiative to go to a nearby convenience store to buy some Shuirong C100. When he returned, he heard Liu Feipeng and a few girls mocking him. (Chinese Brand, or Nongfu Spring Water-Soluble C100, a vitamin drink)

"He didn't just use that as an excuse to run off, did he? The food we ordered is pretty expensive. He probably thought we were splitting the bill, not knowing Dapeng is covering everything tonight." (Rich kid Liu Feipeng)

"Yeah, and going on about how good that cheap drink is. As if we're short on his pocket change."

"Haha, he's such a 'nice guy', you know, even worse than a dog."

The group's burst of laughter made Jiang Nian, who was standing outside the private room, feel awful. He had heard Zhou Yuting's laughter among them. They usually got along well, yet she hadn't said a single word in his defense.

From that moment on, Jiang Nian saw through it all.

Such pseudo-intellectual garbage!

If it hadn't been Zhou Yuting's birthday party, he wouldn't have wanted to go in the first place. In this day and age, pursuing pure love was a fool's errand compared to pursuing pure gold. So what if you're rich, can money buy you a mother?

If he were rich, he wouldn't even spare a glance for someone like Zhou Yuting. He had really been blind before.

Damn it, so that's how they saw me!

"Not going. Let them have fun by themselves," Jiang Nian sneered.

Le Zhi replied, "Alright then, I'll let the great beauty Zhou know."

Jiang Nian put down his phone, leaned back on the sofa, and let out a soft sigh. The world had truly changed. When did good intentions become something to be ridiculed!

His chest heaved up and down. If you have no money, people bully you. If you're rich, whatever you do is right.

The moment his anger peaked, a "ding" sounded in his mind. A translucent panel appeared before his eyes, with lines of white text slowly materializing.

[Age 18: You enrolled in an ordinary second-tier university. After graduation, you joined a large corporation, working so much overtime your liver was about to explode and running so many errands your legs cramped, yet you received no promotion or raise.

Age 28: Your parents, their hearts aching, persuaded you, a man who had accomplished nothing, to go on a blind date. To protect your pride, they carefully handed you a savings book.

Age 30: The bride price was a staggering 588,000. Gritting your teeth, you took out loans for a house and car totaling 1,340,000. The five gold accessories cost 80,000, the filial piety gift 128,000, the in-law address fee 30,000, and the car-entry and exit gifts 66,000.

In a luxurious hotel, guests were as numerous as clouds, with smiles on every face. The bouquet was tossed high into the air, like a white dove flying.

Age 32: The company downsized. You were incredibly lucky to survive the culling. Your supervisor always assigned you the heaviest workload. You came home later and later, your health deteriorating by the day.

Age 35: You lost your job, and your wife grew increasingly dissatisfied with you. You were childless, your medical reports grew worse each time, and your arguments became more frequent.

Age 38: The suitcase wheels rolled across the floor as your wife left with a cold expression. Your shattered phone screen lit up with a call from your parents, ringing incessantly.

Amidst the ruins, you lowered your head and lit a cigarette. Host: Jiang Nian. Divorce Counterattack System loading complete. Do you have... the courage... to begin... your counterattack in life... at this age of forty?]

On the sofa, Jiang Nian stared at the words in his mind, completely stunned.

Divorce? Thirty-eight years old?

Huh?

Wasn't this panel talking about him? The name Jiang Nian was correct. He sat there in a daze for over ten minutes, goosebumps rising all over his skin.

Suddenly, he jerked his head up, realizing something.

"Wait, I'm only eighteen!"

Holy crap, did this system arrive too early?

He looked at the final line of small white text that had frozen on the panel: Do you have... the courage... at this crossroads between thirty and forty... to begin... your counterattack in life?

He reached out his hand, and two choices, "Yes" and "No," faintly appeared.

There was really nothing to hesitate about. If this system was fake, he could just treat it as playing a life-simulation game. If it was real, then he had even less reason to refuse.

Jiang Nian knew very well how humble poverty could make a person. He was relatively lucky; at least if the sky fell, his parents would be there to hold it up. His standard of living wasn't bad.

But what about the future? What if he couldn't provide a sky for his parents to shelter under?

In this world, a person could be incompetent but not broke. Hard work didn't always pay off. If you chose the wrong path, one wrong step would lead to another.

Choice: Yes!

The panel buzzed once, and a new line of text appeared.

[Divorce Counterattack Game loading complete. Host: Jiang Nian. Male. Age: 38.

Your marriage has failed. Standing at the crossroads of forty, you recall the childhood friend of your youth. After you got married, you both cut off all contact, and you never heard from her again.

Re-establish contact with Xu Qianqian. Reward: 300 RMB.]

After reading, Jiang Nian couldn't help but purse his lips. Why was this system so formal and literary?

But that didn't matter, as long as it gave him money.

Re-establish contact with his estranged childhood friend, Xu Qianqian. Hmm... he got up and paced around the living room for a moment. He opened his front door, looked at Xu Qianqian's place across the hall, and fell into deep thought.

Hmm...

Thump thump thump!!!

Jiang Nian knocked on the door with all his might. "Xu Qianqian, what are you doing!?"

After a moment, hurried footsteps sounded from behind the door. Before she even appeared, her crisp voice stabbed through.

"Get lost, Jiang Nian! Are you trying to get yourself killed!?"

Whoosh. The door was pulled open, revealing a small, delicate face puffed up in anger.

A graceful young woman appeared, about 1.6-something meters tall, wearing a beige knitted top, her chest full and round as if hiding a treasure.

The young woman's eyes were lively, her skin fair, her eyebrows like distant mountains, and her smooth long hair was tied back with an elastic band. He'd never noticed before, but she was an absolute budding beauty.

Unfortunately, the two had been at odds since they were kids, and their relationship had deteriorated sharply starting from middle school.

He'd stolen Xu Qianqian's ice cream and "set free" the turtle she was raising in the sewer.

Once, Xu Qianqian had a minor cold, so he swept her up in a princess carry and hauled her to the hospital without letting her get a word in. As a result, she missed an exam, allowing Jiang Nian to achieve first place in class for the one and only time in his life.

For these vile deeds and so many others, he should probably be grateful for the mercy she'd shown in letting him live.

(End of this chapter)
